title: Hebrews Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Hebrews chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Hebrews Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Hebrews Chapter 6.

questions.question: In Hebrews 6, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Leaving the principles of the doctrine of Christ
questions.explanation: This appears first in Hebrews 6:1, where the author encourages leaving the basic principles.

questions.question: What are we encouraged to go on to in Hebrews 6:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Perfection
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:1 states, 'let us go on unto perfection.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:2, which doctrine is mentioned?
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of baptisms
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:2 specifically mentions 'the doctrine of baptisms.'

questions.question: What is said to be impossible in Hebrews 6:4?
options: To renew them again unto repentance
questions.correctAnswer: To renew them again unto repentance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4 states that it is impossible to renew them again unto repentance.

questions.question: What do those who have fallen away do to the Son of God, according to Hebrews 6:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Crucify him again
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:6 mentions that they 'crucify to themselves the Son of God afresh.'

questions.question: What does the earth bring forth that receives blessing from God, as stated in Hebrews 6:7?
questions.correctAnswer: Herbs meet for them
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:7 states that the earth brings forth 'herbs meet for them by whom it is dressed.'

questions.question: What must we lay again according to Hebrews 6:1?
questions.correctAnswer: The foundation of repentance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:1 mentions 'not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works.'

questions.question: What gift have those enlightened tasted of, according to Hebrews 6:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The heavenly gift
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4 states they have 'tasted of the heavenly gift.'

questions.question: What is associated with the doctrine of eternal judgment in Hebrews 6:2?
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection of the dead
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:2 lists 'the resurrection of the dead' as part of the doctrines.

questions.question: What will we do if God permits, according to Hebrews 6:3?
options: Taste the good word of God
questions.correctAnswer: Go on to perfection
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:3 states, 'And this will we do, if God permit,' referring to going on to perfection.

questions.question: Those who fall away are said to put Christ to what, in Hebrews 6:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Open shame
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:6 mentions they 'put him to an open shame.'

questions.question: Is it stated in Hebrews 6 that there is a doctrine of baptisms?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:2 mentions 'the doctrine of baptisms.'

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:5, have those enlightened tasted the good word of God?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:5 states they have 'tasted the good word of God.'

questions.question: Hebrews 6 states that it is impossible for those who fall away to be renewed unto faith.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: While Hebrews 6:4 mentions it is impossible to renew them unto repentance, it does not mention faith specifically.

questions.question: Hebrews 6 states that the earth receives blessings only from the sun.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:7 states the earth receives blessings from God, not just from the sun.

medium.title: Hebrews Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Hebrews Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:8, what is the fate of the earth that bears thorns and briers?
options: It is rejected and near to cursing; its end is to be burned
It is blessed and yields a plentiful harvest
It is watered and nourished by God
It is given to the righteous as an inheritance
questions.correctAnswer: It is rejected and near to cursing; its end is to be burned
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:8 states that the earth which beareth thorns and briers is rejected and is near to cursing; its end is to be burned.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 6:9 promise will happen if someone is persuaded better things and things that accompany salvation as stated in Hebrews 6:8?
options: They are recognized for their better works and salvation
They will be rejected and burned
They will fall away and cannot be renewed
They shall be disciplined by God
questions.correctAnswer: They are recognized for their better works and salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:9 promises that those who are persuaded of better things and things accompanying salvation will be recognized as beloved, in contrast to the rejected earth of verse 8.

questions.question: What reason does Hebrews 6:10 give for God not forgetting your work and labor of love?
options: Because you have ministered to the saints in His name
Because you have fasted and prayed diligently
Because you have kept the law perfectly
questions.correctAnswer: Because you have ministered to the saints in His name
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:10 states that God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labor of love which you have shown toward His name by ministering to the saints.

questions.question: How do Hebrews 6:11 and Hebrews 6:12 relate in terms of Christian living?
options: Verse 11 encourages diligence and full assurance of hope, while verse 12 warns against slothfulness and encourages faith and patience
Verse 11 warns against slothfulness, and verse 12 encourages abandoning hope
Verse 11 commands repentance, while verse 12 promises immediate salvation
Verse 11 speaks of the law, and verse 12 speaks of grace
questions.correctAnswer: Verse 11 encourages diligence and full assurance of hope, while verse 12 warns against slothfulness and encourages faith and patience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:11 exhorts believers to show diligence to the full assurance of hope, and Hebrews 6:12 instructs them not to be slothful but to follow those who inherit promises through faith and patience.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 6:13 reveal about the nature of God's promise to Abraham?
options: God swore by Himself because He could swear by no greater
God promised through angels and prophets
God made a conditional covenant based on Abraham's works
God’s promise was vague and uncertain
questions.correctAnswer: God swore by Himself because He could swear by no greater
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:13 explains that when God made a promise to Abraham, He swore by Himself because there was no greater to swear by.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:14, what specific blessings did God promise to Abraham?
options: Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee
I will give you the land and riches
You will become a great king among nations
questions.correctAnswer: Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:14 quotes God’s promise to Abraham explicitly stating the blessing and multiplication promised to him.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 6:12 encourage believers to live in relation to faith and patience?
options: Be followers of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises
Avoid patience and rely solely on immediate faith
Ignore the promises and live for worldly gain
Be slothful and wait passively for salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Be followers of those who through faith and patience inherit the promises
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:12 urges believers not to be slothful but to imitate those who inherit God's promises through faith and patience.

questions.question: What is the practical application of Hebrews 6:11 regarding Christian hope?
options: To show diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end
To rely on others for salvation
To abandon hope when trials arise
To trust only in works, not hope
questions.correctAnswer: To show diligence to the full assurance of hope unto the end
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:11 encourages believers to demonstrate diligence to the full assurance of hope until the end of their faith journey.

questions.question: What warning is implied by Hebrews 6:6 about falling away after being enlightened?
options: It is impossible to renew them again unto repentance
They will be immediately forgiven without repentance
They can easily return without consequences
They receive a second chance automatically
questions.correctAnswer: It is impossible to renew them again unto repentance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:6 warns that those who have once been enlightened and then fall away cannot be renewed again unto repentance, as they crucify the Son of God afresh.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 6:10 relate to the concept of integrity in Christian service?
options: God does not forget your work and labor of love shown in ministering to saints
God rewards only public displays of service
God ignores acts done in humility
God remembers only sacrifices, not service
questions.correctAnswer: God does not forget your work and labor of love shown in ministering to saints
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:10 teaches that God is just and remembers the sincere work and labor of love done in His name, emphasizing integrity in service.

questions.question: What does Hebrews 6:7 compare to the earth that receives blessing from God?
options: The earth that drinks in the rain and brings forth herbs suitable for those who dress it
The earth that is dry and unproductive
The earth that yields only thorns and briers
The earth that is cursed and burned
questions.correctAnswer: The earth that drinks in the rain and brings forth herbs suitable for those who dress it
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:7 compares blessing to the earth that receives rain and produces useful herbs, symbolizing fruitful believers.

questions.question: How might Hebrews 6:9 encourage a believer struggling with doubt about their standing?
options: It affirms that believers are persuaded of better things and things that accompany salvation
It tells them they are likely to be rejected
It advises them to give up hope
It reminds them that their work is forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that believers are persuaded of better things and things that accompany salvation
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:9 reassures believers that they are considered beloved and that better things and salvation accompany them, encouraging perseverance.

questions.question: What practical lesson about perseverance can be drawn from Hebrews 6:12?
options: Do not be slothful but imitate those who inherit promises through faith and patience
Give up when trials become difficult
Faith alone without patience is sufficient
Patience is unnecessary if faith is strong
questions.correctAnswer: Do not be slothful but imitate those who inherit promises through faith and patience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:12 encourages believers to actively pursue a faithful and patient walk, following examples who inherit God's promises.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 6:10 indicates that God forgets the labor of love shown toward His name.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:10 explicitly states that God is not unrighteous to forget your work and labor of love, indicating He always remembers it.

questions.question: True or False: According to Hebrews 6:6, it is possible for those who have fallen away after being enlightened to be renewed again unto repentance.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:6 states it is impossible for those who have fallen away after enlightenment to be renewed again unto repentance.

hard.title: Hebrews Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Hebrews Chapter 6.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:15, what was the result of Abraham patiently enduring?
questions.correctAnswer: He obtained the promise
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:15 states, 'And so, after he had patiently endured, he obtained the promise.' This shows that endurance led Abraham to receive the promise.

questions.question: Hebrews 6:16 states that men swear by the greater. What is the primary purpose of an oath according to this verse?
options: To bring an end to all strife
questions.correctAnswer: To bring an end to all strife
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:16 says, 'and an oath for confirmation is to them an end of all strife,' indicating that the oath settles disputes.

questions.question: In Hebrews 6:17, why did God confirm His counsel with an oath?
options: To show the immutability of His counsel
questions.correctAnswer: To show the immutability of His counsel
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:17 states, 'God... confirmed it by an oath' to show the unchangeableness (immutability) of His counsel.

questions.question: According to Hebrews 6:18, what are the 'two immutable things' that provide strong consolation?
questions.correctAnswer: God's promise and His oath
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:18 refers to 'two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie,' which are the promise and the oath.

questions.question: Hebrews 6:19 uses a metaphor for hope. What is hope compared to in this verse?
questions.correctAnswer: An anchor of the soul
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:19 states, 'Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast,' making hope an anchor.

questions.question: Who is described as the 'forerunner' who entered within the veil in Hebrews 6:20?
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:20 says, 'Whither the forerunner is for us entered, even Jesus,' identifying Jesus as the forerunner.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἀμεταθετόν' (ametathetón) in Hebrews 6:18 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutable
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:18 uses the word 'ἀμεταθετόν' meaning 'immutable' or 'unchangeable,' describing God's promise and oath.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Hebrews 6:19 when hope is compared to 'an anchor of the soul'?
questions.correctAnswer: Metaphor
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:19 uses metaphor by directly equating hope to 'an anchor of the soul' without using 'like' or 'as.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage is echoed in Hebrews 6:13-14 where God swears by Himself to Abraham?
questions.correctAnswer: Genesis 22:16-17
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:13-14 references God's oath to Abraham, which parallels Genesis 22:16-17 where God swears to bless Abraham.

questions.question: Hebrews 6:20 speaks of Jesus being made a high priest forever after which order?
questions.correctAnswer: The order of Melchisedec
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:20 explicitly states Jesus was made a high priest 'after the order of Melchisedec.'

questions.question: What immediately precedes Hebrews 6:15, which discusses Abraham patiently enduring to obtain the promise?
options: God swearing by Himself to Abraham
A call to leave elementary teachings
questions.correctAnswer: God swearing by Himself to Abraham
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:13-14 directly precede verse 15, describing God making a promise and swearing by Himself to Abraham.

questions.question: Which theme in Hebrews 6:4-6 is most closely related to the concept of apostasy and its consequences?
options: The impossibility of renewing to repentance those who fall away
questions.correctAnswer: The impossibility of renewing to repentance those who fall away
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4-6 warns it is impossible to renew to repentance those who have fallen away after enlightenment.

questions.question: Hebrews 6:7-8 uses agricultural imagery. What is the typological significance of this imagery?
options: It contrasts blessing and judgment based on fruitfulness
It illustrates the seasons of the year
It describes the land of Canaan
questions.correctAnswer: It contrasts blessing and judgment based on fruitfulness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:7-8 compares earth that produces useful herbs receiving blessing versus that which produces thorns and briers facing judgment, typifying blessing and curse.

questions.question: What is the significance of the veil mentioned in Hebrews 6:19 in the context of Old Testament temple worship?
options: It symbolizes the barrier between God and man that Jesus has entered
It refers to the outer court of the temple
It describes the curtain in the holy city of Jerusalem
It denotes a physical veil worn by priests
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the barrier between God and man that Jesus has entered
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:19-20 references the veil in the tabernacle/temple, indicating Jesus as forerunner entered behind it, symbolizing access to God.

questions.question: True or False: Hebrews 6:18 states that it is impossible for God to lie, providing strong consolation to believers.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:18 clearly states it is impossible for God to lie, giving believers strong consolation.

theological.title: Hebrews Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Hebrews Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 6:1 teach about sanctification?
options: Believers should move on from elementary teachings to maturity in Christ
Repentance is unnecessary after initial belief
Perfection is achieved through human effort alone
questions.correctAnswer: Believers should move on from elementary teachings to maturity in Christ
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:1 calls believers to leave behind the basic principles and go on unto perfection, indicating progress in sanctification toward maturity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 6:4 teach about the possibility of falling away?
options: Those enlightened who fall away cannot be renewed to repentance
All believers will inevitably fall away
Falling away is impossible for the truly regenerate
Repentance is always effective to restore any believer
questions.correctAnswer: Those enlightened who fall away cannot be renewed to repentance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4-6 states it is impossible to renew again to repentance those who have been enlightened and then fall away.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 6:10 teach about God's justice in relation to human works?
options: God is just and does not forget the labor of love shown by believers
Human works earn salvation apart from grace
God ignores the works done for His name
Salvation depends solely on human merit
questions.correctAnswer: God is just and does not forget the labor of love shown by believers
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:10 emphasizes God's righteousness in remembering the believers' work and love done toward His name.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 17 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:17 shows God's covenant faithfulness as He confirmed His counsel by an oath to assure the heirs of promise.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Hebrews 6:18 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Immutability
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:18 emphasizes the immutability of God by stating it is impossible for Him to lie.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 6:20 connect to the broader biblical theme of Jesus as High Priest?
options: It affirms Jesus as eternal High Priest in the order of Melchisedec, fulfilling Old Testament typology
It denies Jesus’ priesthood in favor of Levitical priests
It teaches Jesus was a temporary High Priest only during his earthly ministry
It restricts the priesthood to human descendants of Aaron
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms Jesus as eternal High Priest in the order of Melchisedec, fulfilling Old Testament typology
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:20 presents Jesus as a forerunner who entered the heavenly sanctuary, made a high priest forever after Melchisedec’s order, fulfilling the typology in Psalm 110.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 6:7-8 prepare readers for judgment themes later in Scripture?
options: It uses agricultural imagery to illustrate blessing and cursing as results of human response, prefiguring final judgment
It teaches universal salvation without distinction
It suggests judgment is arbitrary and unrelated to works
questions.correctAnswer: It uses agricultural imagery to illustrate blessing and cursing as results of human response, prefiguring final judgment
questions.explanation: Verses 7-8 contrast fruitful earth receiving blessing and earth with thorns receiving curse, symbolizing final judgment.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 13 and 14 teach about God's promises?
options: God’s promises are sure because He swears by Himself, the greatest possible guarantor
God’s promises are conditional on human perfection
God’s promises are uncertain and subject to change
God’s promises depend on angels to enforce them
questions.correctAnswer: God’s promises are sure because He swears by Himself, the greatest possible guarantor
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:13-14 explains that God made a promise to Abraham and confirmed it by an oath swearing by Himself, demonstrating certainty.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 6:19-20 teach about Christian hope and Christ’s priesthood?
options: Hope is an anchor for the soul because Jesus, our forerunner, entered the inner sanctuary as eternal High Priest
Hope is uncertain and fluctuating despite Christ’s priesthood
Jesus is a temporary priest who did not secure hope
Hope is based on human effort apart from Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Hope is an anchor for the soul because Jesus, our forerunner, entered the inner sanctuary as eternal High Priest
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:19-20 links Christian hope as an anchor with Christ’s eternal priesthood and heavenly entry, securing believers’ confidence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 6:4 and 6:6 teach about apostasy and its spiritual consequences?
options: Those who fall away after enlightenment crucify Christ afresh and cannot be renewed to repentance
Apostasy is easily forgiven with no spiritual consequence
Falling away is impossible for true believers
Apostasy only affects outward fellowship, not salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Those who fall away after enlightenment crucify Christ afresh and cannot be renewed to repentance
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4 and 6:6 explain the impossibility of renewing to repentance those who fall away, likening it to crucifying Christ again and putting Him to open shame.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Hebrews 6:4-6 teaches that true believers can lose salvation. What does Hebrews 6:4-6 actually teach?
options: It refers to those who have been enlightened but fall away, indicating a severe apostasy, not necessarily the regenerate
It teaches believers frequently lose salvation and regain it
It claims salvation can be lost by simple doubt
It says all who believe once will definitely fall away
questions.correctAnswer: It refers to those who have been enlightened but fall away, indicating a severe apostasy, not necessarily the regenerate
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:4-6 warns of the impossibility of renewal for those who fall away after enlightenment, often interpreted as a warning against apostasy rather than casual believers losing salvation.

questions.question: What doctrine does Hebrews 6:12 teach about perseverance in the Christian life?
options: Believers are called to imitate those who inherit promises through faith and patience
Perseverance is unnecessary if faith is present
Inheritance of promises is guaranteed without effort
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are called to imitate those who inherit promises through faith and patience
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:12 exhorts believers to be diligent and avoid slothfulness by following faithful and patient exemplars who inherit God’s promises.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated in Hebrews 6:10 regarding God's awareness of human deeds?
questions.correctAnswer: Righteousness
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:10 states God is not unrighteous to forget the labor of love, showing His attribute of righteousness and justice.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Hebrews 6:2 and 6:20 teach about eschatology and Christ’s role?
options: The resurrection and eternal judgment are linked with Christ’s eternal high priesthood in the heavenly sanctuary
Eschatology is unrelated to Christ’s priesthood
The resurrection is symbolic, not literal
Eternal judgment is based on human works alone
questions.correctAnswer: The resurrection and eternal judgment are linked with Christ’s eternal high priesthood in the heavenly sanctuary
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:2 lists resurrection and eternal judgment as doctrines, while 6:20 shows Christ as high priest in heaven, linking these eschatological realities with His priestly ministry.

questions.question: How does Hebrews 6:11 contribute to the doctrine of assurance of hope?
options: Believers are urged to show diligence to the full assurance of hope until the end
Assurance of hope is unattainable in this life
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are urged to show diligence to the full assurance of hope until the end
questions.explanation: Hebrews 6:11 exhorts believers to be diligent so they may maintain full assurance of hope to the end of their faith journey.
